title: Pre-trial sensorimotor theta–beta phase–amplitude coupling vs mu/beta ERD for motor-imagery class prediction in eegmmidbg (independent-set AUC 0.549 vs 0.462)
abstract: Question: does the sensorimotor-cortical phase–amplitude coupling between the rest immediately preceding a motor-imagery trial — sensorimotor beta-band envelope weighted by instantaneous theta-phase (pac_theta_beta) — predict the trial class (T1/T2) better than the standard mu/beta event-related desynchronization (ERD) during the trial? Datasets: eegmmidbg (PhysioNet, Open Access, byte-verified), local subjects S001–S004 (6 files, 90 MI trials) and independent subjects S005–S008 (16 files, 240 MI trials). Features per trial: standard — mu/beta ERD (7.5–12.5 / 15.5–25.5 Hz) during the MI trial vs the preceding rest; novel — sensorimotor-ROI theta–beta phase–amplitude coupling of the pre-trial rest (vector strength of beta-envelope phases weighted by theta phase), plus pre-trial rest theta, beta, gamma and spectral-entropy features. Outcome: trial class (T1/T2). Evaluation: Mann-Whitney AUCs with bootstrap 95% CIs; 5-fold stratified balanced-accuracy LDA on standardized features; label-shuffle falsification; cross-dataset transfer (LDA trained on local, tested on independent). Results: local AUCs — erd_mu 0.474, erd_beta 0.605, pac_theta_beta 0.556; independent AUCs — erd_mu 0.427, erd_beta 0.462, pac_theta_beta 0.549. Claim: on the independent dataset, AUC(pac_theta_beta) − AUC(erd_beta) ≥ +0.05 (pre-stated prediction); observed +0.087 (bootstrap CIs overlap; local difference −0.049). LDA CV independent: standard 0.503, novel [pac] 0.555. Honest scope: small local N (90) and the independent set is disjoint subjects of the same source; the proposed pattern does not beat the standard ERD by a meaningful margin.
